claims.text: Identifying sources of uncertainty in large language models is an important step toward improving reliability, trustworthiness, and interpretability.
Input clarification ensembling is an uncertainty decomposition framework for LLMs that can be applied to any pre-trained LLM.

When aleatoric uncertainty arises from ambiguity or under-specification in LLM inputs, input clarification ensembling makes it possible to factor predictions into separate aleatoric and epistemic terms using a Bayesian-like decomposition.
Input clarification ensembling provides accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification on several language processing tasks.

evidence.description: The approach generates a set of clarifications for the input, feeds them into an LLM, and ensembles the corresponding predictions.
Empirical evaluations on several language processing tasks demonstrate accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification.

methodologies.name: Input Clarification Ensembling
methodologies.description: A framework that generates input clarifications, feeds them to a pre-trained LLM, and ensembles the predictions to separate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.

limitations.text: Identifying sources of uncertainty in large language models remains an important open research question.
